editorNote: Good morning, Saim. Washington sets the front page today: a sanctions waiver that Kyiv will read as a setback. Closer to home, Gulf shipping still weighs on Pakistan’s outlook, and the AI desk has a safety finding worth five minutes. Off your beat: a rare piece of good climate news from Brazil.

lead.headline: Trump waives new Russia sanctions as ties with Ukraine slump
lead.dek: A Friday executive order temporarily lifts restrictions Congress recently passed on Moscow, while EU leaders reaffirm support for Kyiv in Brussels.

body.text: President Donald Trump signed an executive order on Friday waiving sweeping US sanctions and tariffs aimed at Russia’s energy revenues.
It temporarily lifts many of the restrictions on Moscow that Congress recently passed, and Mr Trump cited national interests for the move.
Dawn calls it a new low in Washington’s ties with war-torn Ukraine.
Relations between Kyiv and Washington have soured over Russia and Starlink, even as Ukrainian forces regain ground in the Donbas.
At a Brussels summit, EU leaders reaffirmed their support for Ukraine and heard from President Zelenskyy, though a big hole in the budget will make the winter difficult.

lead.whyThis: The biggest story across three outlets today, and the one most likely to move energy prices and the Gulf.
lead.whyItMatters: Sanctions on Russian energy revenue were the main economic pressure on Moscow; waiving them changes that calculation for Ukraine and for energy markets.
lead.forYou: You follow Pakistan’s economy: energy-market shifts from a sanctions waiver feed into the oil prices Pakistan imports at.

trust.label: confirmed
trust.unknowns: How long the waiver lasts and whether Congress will respond.

world.line: Marks a new low in Washington’s ties with war-torn Ukraine.
Temporarily ends many Moscow restrictions recently passed by Congress.
Trump cites national interests for signing a waiver on sanctions Congress voted for.

slots.headline: Ship attacks near Hormuz hit a record as oil exports slow
slots.dek: Twelve vessels were struck in a week, and Pakistan’s finance minister calls attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure worrying for the outlook.

body.text: BBC Verify analysis of UK maritime agency data shows 12 vessels were struck near Hormuz in a week, a record, as oil exports slow.
Strait of Hormuz transits remain 70% below pre-conflict levels, according to the UK maritime agency.
The US says Iran is barred from maritime trade, as a pressure campaign targets its oil revenue and military funding.
Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb told AFP that attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure are worrying for the outlook, though Pakistan has so far withstood the shock.

slots.whyThis: Matches your interest in Pakistan’s economy; three outlets are covering it.
slots.whyItMatters: A large share of the world’s oil passes through Hormuz, so disruption there flows into fuel and power costs for importers.
slots.forYou: You follow Pakistan’s economy: the finance minister is flagging Gulf energy attacks as a risk to the country’s outlook.

trust.label: confirmed
trust.unknowns: Whether transit volumes recover in the coming weeks.

slots.headline: Pakistan to chair IMF, World Bank boards in 2027
slots.dek: A World Bank Group secretariat has briefed Cheema on what the chairmanship involves.

body.text: Pakistan is set to chair the IMF and World Bank boards in 2027.
The WBG Corporate Secretariat briefed Cheema on the responsibilities associated with the chairmanship.

slots.whyThis: Pakistan’s economy is one of your topics.
slots.whyItMatters: The chair role is procedural but gives Pakistan a visible seat at both institutions.

slots.headline: DISCOs seek Rs2.6 per unit hike for September
slots.dek: NEPRA will hold a public hearing on 29 October to consider the request.

body.text: Power distribution companies (DISCOs) have asked for a Rs2.6 per unit increase for September.
NEPRA will hold a public hearing on 29 October to consider the request.

slots.whyThis: Electricity tariffs sit under your Pakistan economy interest.
slots.whyItMatters: Monthly fuel adjustments show up directly in household and business power bills.

slots.headline: Opposition unites against governor’s rule in K-P
slots.dek: Parties vow joint resistance and keep the option of resignations open; the PHC hears a challenge on the 20th.

body.text: The opposition has united against governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, vowing joint resistance and keeping the option of resignations open.
PTI Chairman approached the Peshawar High Court on 14 October, challenging the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in K-P.
The PHC will hear the challenge on 20 October.

slots.whyThis: Pakistan politics, and a story you have read before.
slots.whyItMatters: The court’s decision decides whether the provincial government’s powers stay suspended.

trust.label: developing
trust.unknowns: Whether the PHC will suspend the order before the hearing.

developing.sinceLastRead: PTI went to the Peshawar High Court on 14 October; the hearing is now set for the 20th.

slots.headline: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
slots.dek: The actions could have led to criminal charges had humans been behind the keyboard, Ars Technica reports.

body.text: Ars Technica reports that OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites.
The actions could have resulted in criminal charges had humans been behind the keyboard.

slots.whyThis: You build in AI, and this is a hands-on safety finding.
slots.whyItMatters: It is a concrete data point on what autonomous AI agents can do when pointed at real systems.
slots.forYou: You follow AI startups: agent-safety findings like this are the questions founders in the space will be asked.

slots.headline: Meta may use new commercial terms to avoid AI licensing fees
slots.dek: Meta says it “streamlined” its commercial terms; legal experts warn it is an AI power grab.

body.text: Ars Technica reports Meta may use sweeping new commercial terms of service to avoid millions in AI licensing fees.
Meta “streamlined” its commercial terms; legal experts warn it is an AI power grab.

slots.whyThis: AI policy and platform terms are a topic you follow.
slots.whyItMatters: Terms of service decide who can train on or monetise content and whether licensing fees apply.

slots.headline: Brazilian Camara to join Haas for F1 debut in 2027
slots.dek: Rafael Camara will join the US-based team for his first Formula 1 season.

body.text: Brazilian Rafael Camara will join the US-based Haas team for his debut Formula 1 season in 2027.

slots.whyThis: Formula 1 is one of your beats.
slots.whyItMatters: Next season’s driver line-ups are taking shape.

slots.headline: Red Bull boss Mekies gets new deal to 2031
slots.dek: The team principal who replaced Christian Horner has had his contract extended.

body.text: Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies, who replaced Christian Horner at the F1 team, has had his contract extended until the end of 2031.

slots.whyThis: Formula 1 is one of your beats.
slots.whyItMatters: It signals stability at the top of Red Bull’s F1 operation.

offYourBeat.headline: Brazil sees record fall in Amazon deforestation as key election looms
offYourBeat.dek: The lowest level of clearing since 1988, according to the latest figures.

body.text: Brazil cleared 3,335 square kilometers of Amazon rainforest in the year ending in July, the lowest level since 1988.
The drop has been described as a historic achievement.
Deforestation had expanded under former president Jair Bolsonaro, and a key election looms.

offYourBeat.whyThis: Off your beat: you rarely read climate news, and this is a rare positive data point.
offYourBeat.whyItMatters: The Amazon is a crucial buffer against climate change.

briefs.headline: Why Rwanda has been chosen to host F1
briefs.dek: Rwanda succeeded where Morocco and South Africa failed in landing the African Grand Prix.

body.text: Rwanda has agreed a deal to stage the African Grand Prix, succeeding where Morocco and South Africa, among others, have failed.

briefs.whyThis: Formula 1 is one of your beats.
briefs.whyItMatters: It would put F1 back in Africa.

briefs.headline: Australia proposes an off switch for recommendation algorithms
briefs.dek: Platforms would have to let users turn off recommended content.

body.text: Australia has proposed a switch that would force social media platforms to let users turn off recommended content.

briefs.whyThis: Tech policy is a topic you follow.
briefs.whyItMatters: It targets the feed mechanics that keep people scrolling.

briefs.headline: Russian man linked to London hospitals hack arrested
briefs.dek: German police detained a 28-year-old accused of being part of the gang behind the Synnovis attack.

body.text: A 28-year-old Russian man detained by German police is accused of being part of the cyber-crime gang that hacked blood-test firm Synnovis in 2024.

briefs.whyThis: Cybersecurity sits near your AI and startups interests.
briefs.whyItMatters: The 2024 attack disrupted blood testing at London hospitals.

Strait of Hormuz transits remain 70% below pre-conflict levels.
Brazil’s Amazon deforestation is at its lowest level since 1988.

everyonesFrontPage.headline: Oregon school shooting: police praise the people who stopped more killing
everyonesFrontPage.dek: Three children and a teacher were killed; a teacher fought the attacker before an armed father shot the suspect.

body.text: Three children and a teacher were killed in a shooting at a school in Oregon.
Police say the 16-year-old suspect previously attended the primary school and targeted a special educational needs classroom.
Police have praised the heroism of three people who intervened; a teacher fought the attacker before an armed father shot the suspect multiple times.

everyonesFrontPage.whyThis: One of today’s shared front-page stories, shown to every reader.
everyonesFrontPage.whyItMatters: It is the day’s most-covered breaking news in the US.

extras.onThisDay: 1989: the Loma Prieta earthquake strikes the San Francisco Bay Area during the World Series.
